clue.text: Fancies taking top off for pay

indicators.note: removing the top of a down entry means its first letter is dropped from the synonym of the first word

parts.note: fancies, as a plural noun, are longings or yearnings

explanation.surface: Someone is told to give up their fancies in exchange for a wage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking top off' removes the first letter, Y, from YEARNINGS.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnings are the money a person is paid for work, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: It may produce cry sucking end of thumb

definitions.text: It may produce cry sucking end of thumb

indicators.note: sucking means drawing something in, so the cry word takes a letter inside it

parts.note: to bay is the cry of a hound, so a bay is a cry

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word thumb

explanation.surface: An infant sucking its thumb is the kind of thing that may set up a wail.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer and builds it: 'sucking' puts B, the last letter of 'thumb', inside BAY.
explanation.definitionFit: An infant is the classic producer of crying and the classic thumb-sucker, so the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Member caught in 'yes' vote for heritage

parts.note: a limb or member of the body, such as a leg

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for caught within the vote word

parts.note: ay (or aye) is a vote in favour, as in Parliament
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A politician caught voting yes, it seems, for a heritage bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts C inside AY.
explanation.definitionFit: A legacy is something handed down from the past, which is what heritage means.

clue.text: Crowd's rising frenzy catching first person in nuptials

indicators.note: rising in a down entry means the crowd word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to crowd is to ram or cram; the 's is read as 'is'

indicators.note: catching means holding something inside, so the frenzy word takes the pronoun within it

parts.note: a frenzy of anger is a rage
I is the first-person pronoun

explanation.surface: A crowd's rising frenzy grips the first person at a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crowd's' reads as 'crowd is', with crowd the verb (to ram or cram), not the noun; 'rising' turns that word upward, as this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuptials is a formal word for a wedding, the ceremony of joining in wedlock.

clue.text: Beam seeing hypocrisy current party promoted

parts.note: cant is insincere, hypocritical talk
I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: promoted means raised up, so in a down entry the party word is read upwards

parts.note: a revel is a lively party

explanation.surface: The setter, Beam, catches sight of hypocrisy as a current party is promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: Beam is the setter's own name, used here as the definition. 'promoted' turns REVEL into LEVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantilever is a projecting beam or girder fixed at one end only, as in cantilever bridges.

clue.text: Swathe of love embraced by company do

indicators.note: embraced by means held inside, so the zero letter sits within the swindle word

parts.note: to do someone is to swindle or con them
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: A swathe of affection wrapped up by a company party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'do' looks like a party but means to cheat; 'embraced by' puts O inside CON.
explanation.definitionFit: To swathe is to wrap up closely, as a silkworm wraps itself in its silk casing.

clue.text: Bird, domesticated, possessing a comb

indicators.note: possessing means holding, so the tame word contains the other pieces

parts.note: a pet is a tame, domesticated animal
to rake is to comb through, and a rake is a kind of comb for soil

explanation.surface: A tame bird with a crest or comb on its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comb' suggests a bird's crest, but here it is the garden tool's action, to rake.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a small, long-tailed parrot, an example of a bird kept as a cage pet.

clue.text: One has Mass supporting article of faith

indicators.note: in a down entry, supporting means placed below, so the article sits on top

parts.note: the definite article is the word the
one is the Roman numeral I
's is a contraction of has, as in he's got
M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

explanation.surface: Holding Mass as a central article of one's faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One has' is read as I'S; 'supporting' puts I, S and M beneath THE.
explanation.definitionFit: Theism is belief in a god or gods, a religious faith as opposed to atheism.

clue.text: River running through Panama zone

indicators.note: running through means the answer passes through the letters of these words, which contain it

explanation.surface: A river flows across a Panamanian zone.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is in PanAMA ZONE.
explanation.definitionFit: The great South American river is the largest in the world by volume of water.

clue.text: Sole working lavatory's vacant

parts.note: a machine that is on is working

indicators.note: vacant means emptied, so just the outer letters of the lavatory word remain

parts.note: the 's here is read as 'is', linking to vacant

explanation.surface: A notice: the one functioning toilet is free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vacant' empties LAVATORY to LY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sole and only both mean single, the one and no other, as in an only child.

clue.text: Wandering Mariner's Rime recalled empty supply

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor or mariner; the 's links

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the two letters are read in reverse
empty means the inside letters are removed, leaving only the outer letters of the word Rime

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allowance or supply

explanation.surface: Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner recalled as an empty supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves RE from RIME and 'recalled' reverses it to ER.
explanation.definitionFit: An aberration is a departure or straying from the normal course, hence a wandering.

clue.text: Bond maybe accepts knock over being fashionable

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so the agent word holds the other piece

parts.note: James Bond is an example of a spy

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the criticism word is reversed

parts.note: to pan or knock is to criticise harshly

explanation.surface: James Bond takes a knock while staying stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knock' is to criticise (pan), not a blow; 'over' turns it round before 'accepts' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A snappy dresser is smart and stylish, so the word is a synonym for fashionable.

clue.text: Snooped around base before midnight in secret

indicators.note: around means the snooping word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to pry is to snoop, so snooped is pried

indicators.note: before puts the base word ahead of the midnight letter

parts.note: base means low or vile
the middle letter of night is G

explanation.surface: Someone snooped around a military base just before midnight, all in secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' is read as the middle of 'night', a standard trick; 'base' means low, not a military site.
explanation.definitionFit: Privileged information is confidential, given in confidence and so kept from others.

clue.text: Bird watching 'gripping' first of larks

indicators.note: gripping means holding fast, so the watching word holds the letter inside

parts.note: staring means watching intently

indicators.note: first of picks out the opening letter of the word larks

explanation.surface: A bird caught by a spectator who grips the leading lark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gripping' puts L inside STARING.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common speckled songbird that gathers in great murmuring flocks.

clue.text: Bit starter of smooth foie gras?

indicators.note: starter of picks out the opening letter of the word smooth

parts.note: foie gras is fattened goose or duck liver, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: A little starter of smooth foie gras on a restaurant plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bit' looks like part of the menu scene but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A sliver is a small thin piece, such as a sliver of cake or glass.

clue.text: View of frozen water summit on air

indicators.note: on air means as broadcast, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: frozen water is ice; a summit is the height or top of a mountain

explanation.surface: A view of a frozen peak described on a radio broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: ICE HEIGHT spoken quickly gives the answer's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesight is the power of seeing, and one's view is what that faculty takes in.

clue.text: Hoists part of roof on hotel

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the roof word follows the hotel letter

parts.note: Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the eaves are the overhanging lower edges of a roof

explanation.surface: Builders hoist a section of roof onto a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave something is to lift it with effort, as one hoists a heavy load.

clue.text: Guard present in electric blankets

indicators.note: blankets means covers or contains, so these words contain the answer within them

explanation.surface: A security guard is on duty in a warehouse full of electric blankets.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is in preSENT IN ELectric.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentinel is a soldier or guard posted to keep watch, a sentry.

clue.text: Capital couple of articles on Poles

indicators.note: in a down entry, on means placed above, so the articles sit on top of the poles

parts.note: A is the indefinite article and the is the definite article
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Two newspaper pieces written about Polish people in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the capital city of Greece, named after the goddess Athena.

clue.text: Incumbent Trump possibly losing head?

indicators.note: losing head means the first letter is cut off the president word

parts.note: Donald Trump is an example of a president

explanation.surface: Might the sitting president be about to lose his head?
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' drops P from PRESIDENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident is one who holds a post on site, as an incumbent occupies an office or home.

clue.text: The woman rings officer up for dates

indicators.note: up in a down entry means the whole is read from the bottom
rings means surrounds, so the woman word goes around the officer word

parts.note: the woman is she
a cop is a police officer

explanation.surface: A woman phones a police officer to arrange a date.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rings' means surrounds rather than telephones; 'up' reverses the whole result, as this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Epochs are periods or eras of history, and dates can mean historical periods.

clue.text: One might be coming or going

definitions.text: One might be coming or going

parts.words: One might be coming or going
parts.note: the -ing words named are verbal nouns, as in 'going is hard'

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a confused person not knowing whether coming or going; in grammar the two words are examples of a part of speech.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar this is a verb form ending in -ing used as a noun, as with swimming in 'swimming is fun'.

clue.text: Mark, perhaps, try and arrange letters — one's missing

parts.note: a go is a try or attempt

indicators.note: one's missing means a single repeated letter is lost from the spelling word

parts.note: to spell is to arrange letters into a word

explanation.surface: Try to arrange the letters for a word with one missing, as in a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's missing' drops one of the two Ls from SPELL.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark's is one of the four books of the New Testament telling Christ's life, so it exemplifies the type.

clue.text: Solitude of drink — Venetian dismissing outsiders in bar …

indicators.note: in places the drink and the trimmed screen inside the except word

parts.note: bar means except, as does less
one, as in 'a quick one', is a drink

indicators.note: dismissing outsiders means removing the outer letters of the window-screen word

parts.note: a Venetian is a kind of window blind made of slats

explanation.surface: A lonely drinker finds solitude, a Venetian shut out of the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Venetian' stands for a Venetian blind, a slatted window screen, and 'dismissing outsiders' trims it. 'bar' is the preposition meaning except, not a pub, and 'in' places the drink and trimmed screen inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Loneliness and solitude both mean the state of being alone without company.

clue.text: … gave expression of one having miserable exterior

indicators.note: having means holding, so the numeral is held by the other word
exterior says the miserable word is on the outside of the numeral

parts.note: miserable means sad
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Continuing the bar scene: the lonely drinker spoke with a gloomy face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having' and 'exterior' put SAD around I.
explanation.definitionFit: To have said something is to have voiced or expressed it in words.

clue.text: Drink essence of tasty syrup

indicators.note: essence means the heart, so the central letter of tasty is taken

parts.note: in Cockney rhyming slang, syrup of figs means wig

explanation.surface: Drinking the very essence of a tasty syrup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'syrup' is Cockney rhyming slang (rhymes standing for words): 'syrup of figs' rhymes with wig.
explanation.definitionFit: A swig is a large gulp of a drink, and as a verb to swig is to drink deeply.

clue.text: Flail about in the endless quiet

indicators.note: in places the concerning word within the other letters
endless means the final letter of the word the is cut off

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone thrashes about in endless silence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims only 'the'; 'in' puts the concerning word between the trimmed article and the call for quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: To thresh is to beat grain with a flail, so the verb flail describes the same action.

clue.text: Type of small rodents put back inside cage

indicators.note: inside places the reversed rodents within the enclosure word

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure or cage for animals

indicators.note: put back means reversed, so the rodent word is read backwards

parts.note: mice are small rodents

explanation.surface: A scientist puts small rodents back inside their cage for study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Type' looks like a classifying word in the surface but is the definition: a sample or example.
explanation.definitionFit: A specimen is an example or sample representing a type, as in a specimen of a species.
